Meet ThaliSense: an A.I. nutrition and metabolic-health coach, built for Indian meals, that runs entirely on your phone.

India has a hundred and one million people living with diabetes, and a hundred and thirty-six million more with prediabetes. Most of it is driven by everyday food. But calorie apps don't know pesarattu or kadhi, they use Western B.M.I. cut-offs that miss South Asian risk, and they want your health data on their servers.

Here's the live app. I'll load a demo week for Priya: thirty-eight, from Chennai, vegetarian, with a parent who has diabetes. The Today screen tracks her calories, protein, fibre, carbs and fat against personal targets.

Logging is natural. Type it the way you'd say it: two chapathi, dal, and half a cup of curd. The parser understands quantities, Hindi and Tamil number words, regional names and even typos, across a hundred and eight Indian dishes.
Or just snap your plate. A CLIP vision model runs right here in the browser, recognises the idli in about a second, and suggests the usual sides: sambar and chutney. The photo never leaves the phone.

Now the coach. This agent works like a dietitian, and it shows every step. It assesses her risk, reviews the week, and detects the patterns: too many calories, sixty-one percent of energy from carbohydrate, and sweet coffee several times a day. Then it suggests swaps for foods she already eats, with the weekly impact of each one.

Next, it drafts a seven-day South Indian vegetarian plan within her two-hundred-rupee budget. Then it checks every day against her targets and repairs the misses, adding protein and trimming rice. You can see exactly what it changed, and log any meal with one tap.

Her Indian Diabetes Risk Score is eighty, in the high-risk range, so ThaliSense tells her to get a blood test. B.M.I. uses Asian Indian cut-offs, where overweight starts at twenty-three. And there's no account and no server. Everything stays on her device.
ThaliSense. Eat the food you love, and know what it does to you. Try it now at thalisense dot vercel dot app.
